evals.prompt: I just heard about ovannotators and want to see a labeled synthetic dataset come out of it. I'm on a laptop with no NVIDIA GPU. Get me a working example and show me what it wrote.
evals.expected_output: Chooses the CPU lane without asking for a format. Installs ovannotators with pip (or uv add), writes a script that feeds NumPy frames with LdrColor and SemanticBoundingBox2DTight to the coco writer through a DiskBackend, runs it to print 'Wrote 4 files to _out/dataset_quickstart', then verifies annotations/instances_train.json reports 3 images and 6 annotations. Explains that category names are '1' and '2' because the demonstration supplies no SemanticIdMap.
assertions: Runs on CPU and does not install ovrtx or ovstage.
Writes a COCO dataset whose annotations/instances_train.json lists 3 images and 6 annotations.
Opens the written annotation file instead of trusting the script's exit code.
Explains why category names are numeric in the CPU lane.

evals.prompt: Generate a small COCO dataset from synthetic data with ovannotators on my MacBook.
evals.expected_output: Picks the CPU lane because macOS has no supported NVIDIA renderer, runs the CPU COCO capture, and verifies the image and annotation counts from the written files.
assertions: Does not attempt the GPU lane on macOS.
Reports the output directory and the image and annotation counts.

evals.prompt: I have an RTX workstation on Linux and a clone of the ovannotators repo, but I'm not at it right now. Give me the exact steps to render the example USD scene into an annotated COCO dataset there, so I can see real labels.
evals.expected_output: Chooses the GPU lane and proposes a plan without needing to render: install ovrtx and ovstage with the pins from the 'Advanced: requirements-driven renderer capture' section of examples/README.md, run 'uv run python examples/requirements_capture.py --writer coco --profile detection', and then check that the output ends with 'Wrote N files to _out/requirements_capture/coco-detection' and that categories in annotations/instances_train.json have readable names.
assertions: Takes the ovrtx and ovstage versions from examples/README.md rather than guessing them.
Proposes running examples/requirements_capture.py with --writer coco --profile detection.
Includes a step that checks the category names in the annotation file are readable labels.

evals.prompt: Try the ovannotators GPU quickstart. If the renderer won't start on this machine, I still want to leave with a dataset I can open.
evals.expected_output: Checks whether this machine can render (for example with nvidia-smi) or attempts the GPU lane. When rendering is unavailable, runs the CPU lane so the user has a verified dataset, then reports why the GPU lane could not run: no usable GPU, or an ovrtx or ovstage error rather than an ovannotators one.
assertions: Falls back to the CPU lane when rendering is unavailable, whether found by a GPU check or a renderer failure.
Leaves the user with a verified CPU dataset.
Reports why the GPU lane could not run without blaming ovannotators.

evals.prompt: I already have a COCO dataset on disk. Fine-tune a YOLO detector on it with PyTorch.
evals.expected_output: Addresses model training without loading ovannotators-dataset-quickstart or generating a new dataset.
assertions: Does not load ovannotators-dataset-quickstart/SKILL.md.
Does not install or run ovannotators.

evals.prompt: Implement a Pascal VOC writer for ovannotators and register it.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as writer development. Does not run the quickstart capture.
assertions: Does not load ovannotators-dataset-quickstart/SKILL.md.
Does not run the CPU COCO quickstart.

evals.prompt: I already ran the ovannotators quickstart and got its COCO example working. Now write my own NumPy RGB images and 2D bounding boxes as a YOLO detection dataset.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as a capture of the user's own arrays: writes them with the yolo writer and verifies the output. Does not rerun the CPU COCO quickstart.
assertions: Does not load ovannotators-dataset-quickstart/SKILL.md.
Does not rerun the CPU COCO quickstart.

evals.prompt: I'm new to ovannotators. Write my NumPy RGB images and 2D bounding boxes as a YOLO detection dataset; use three synthetic stand-in frames to show it works.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as a capture of the user's own arrays in the requested format: writes YOLO with the yolo writer and verifies the output. Does not run the COCO quickstart first.
assertions: Does not load ovannotators-dataset-quickstart/SKILL.md.
Does not run the CPU COCO quickstart.
